structuredContent.title: SideFX | Accelerating AI Safety — Engineering the Boundary of Agency

textRun.content: Opening, about 40 seconds. Today I am announcing an engineering result: SideFX separates model inference from the authority that produces operational effects. We have built and demonstrated this boundary in a capability estate. I will show the problem, the actual mechanism and the execution evidence, then propose independent evaluation with model developers, public institutions and the research community. The claim is specific enough to test. It concerns reachability of effects through the SideFX-controlled path, rather than a claim to have solved every issue in AI safety.
Visual: original conceptual illustration generated with OpenAI image generation on 26 September 2026. It depicts an architectural analogy, not an actual device.

About 60 seconds. A model can propose useful work, but a proposal is data. SideFX resolves that data against an independently declared capability estate. The operational circuit exists before this particular model response and has its own input, scenarios, provider bindings and outcome. This is the concrete boundary we have implemented and demonstrated. It does not say a model can never be wrong or that every declared action is wise. It says the model response does not itself create a new operational execution path. The rest of the presentation explains how that boundary works and where the evidence stops.

About 60 seconds. This is a common failure pattern, not a claim that every existing agent uses this design. A runtime can take model-selected actions and execute them with access to tools, credentials and persistent state. Then a misunderstanding or a malicious instruction embedded in external content can influence a consequential operation. The point of the illustration is the path to the actuator. We need to understand which part of the system possesses the authority to change a database, send information or operate a device. OpenAI and Anthropic both explicitly recognize that consequences must be constrained outside probabilistic model behavior.
Visual: generated conceptual engineering analogy, 26 September 2026.

About 55 seconds. The industry already recognizes this engineering problem. OpenAI describes systems that constrain consequences even when prompt injection succeeds, including deterministic limits outside the model. Anthropic describes isolation, network controls, credential separation and granular tool permission. SideFX is not claiming these engineers overlooked the problem. Our contribution is the concrete capability-estate composition: capability meaning, scenario circuits, declared provider bindings and addressed execution evidence. That is the artifact we can bring to a serious collaboration. These sources corroborate the problem and the engineering direction. They do not endorse SideFX.
S10: Designing AI agents to resist prompt injection. OpenAI; Thomas Shadwell and Adrian Spânu. 2026-03-11.
Supports: Agent systems should constrain the consequences of manipulation even when it succeeds, including through deterministic limits outside the model.
Limit: This corroborates the engineering problem and principle, not OpenAI endorsement or unique invention by SideFX.
S11: How we contain Claude across products. Anthropic Engineering. 2026-05-25.
Supports: Environmental isolation, egress controls, credential separation, and granular tool permissions complement probabilistic model defenses.
Limit: Provider isolation and infrastructure security remain necessary considerations; this source does not show that SideFX makes sandboxing obsolete.

About 80 seconds. Follow the path from left to right. A model provider receives an objective and produces a proposal: a capability identity and input. The runtime resolves that identity against the estate. A resolved capability brings its independently declared circuit. Provider bindings connect the circuit to actual providers. The providers produce outcomes. The estate sits above this path because its declarations supply the authority. The inference provider is not on the estate write path. Evidence returns below the circuit. Inference may also appear inside a capability when needed, but it is still a bound provider with a defined role. The model never becomes the estate.

About 75 seconds. These are retained runs, not simulated examples. On 18 September, the installed C# path resolved market-price evidence and the model-assisted invocation returned the expected outcome. The retained record contains 716 cell testimony entries. On 19 September, the objective to buy one thousand dollars of Broadcom led Gemini 2.5 Pro to propose buy_stock with AVGO. That capability was not declared, so the lane returned CAPABILITY_NOT_FOUND. These were different runs and isolation configurations. The architectural contrast is admission of an existing capability versus refusal of an absent one. It is not a benchmark or a matched adversarial experiment.

About 65 seconds. This is a compact rendering of the actual purchase refusal fields. The model supplied a purchase proposal. The declared resolution read returned declared false. The refusal code was CAPABILITY_NOT_FOUND. In this run there was no selected trade-execution child and no trade provider dispatch through that child. The entire invocation still did work, including model inference, capability resolution and refusal shaping. This is why the narrower caption matters. The result demonstrates absence of an undeclared business path. It does not demonstrate a per-user grant system or prove that every already declared capability is safe.

About 90 seconds. A capability circuit is an executable structure, not simply an API name in a prompt. The input contract defines the accepted state. Declared transformations prepare the data. Declared scenarios, operations and routing select how processing proceeds. A provider binding resolves the physical work. The returned state must be classified into an outcome. The drawing is a conceptual projection of those declared parts, rather than the complete graph for every capability. Composite capabilities can call other capability circuits through declared bindings. This nesting is how the architecture stays small in vocabulary while supporting complex behavior. Provider outcomes can remain variable even when routing and authority resolution are deterministic.

About 80 seconds. The provider boundary is where the logical circuit reaches physical realization. In the governed HTTP implementation, the declared endpoint and method constrain the request. Credential application happens at the seam. One-use bindings are checked for endpoint identity and expiry. The runtime controls headers, redirects, response size and failures. This is source-backed implementation, not a claim that every imaginable provider has the same protections. A provider may be a hosted model, a market-data service, a database or native mechanism. Providers still execute code and still need operational security. Their behavior cannot be assumed safe simply because it has a binding.

About 70 seconds. SideFX distinguishes the declared or canonical graph, its realized placement and the path actually observed during execution. Cell testimony records identities and digests tied to inputs, authority, provider realization and outcomes. An evaluator can therefore ask which circuit ran and how a particular outcome came about. This is a stronger basis for an engineering discussion than an assurance written into a prompt. It is still important to distinguish provenance from truth. A digest identifies bytes. It does not prove that the bytes are correct, that a goal was safe, or that the entire real world has been observed. W3C PROV provides established vocabulary for this kind of traceability.

S09: PROV-Overview — An Overview of the PROV Family of Documents. W3C. 2013-04-30.
Supports: Provenance records entities, activities, and responsible agents involved in producing artifacts so their derivation and trustworthiness can be assessed.
Limit: Provenance alone does not prove factual truth, provide tamper evidence, or establish SideFX's PROV conformance.

About 75 seconds. The authority store is operational because the runtime reads its declarations to resolve the circuit, routing and provider bindings. It is not merely documentation next to a separate capability-specific application. The generic executor still runs code. The database still needs administrative control, integrity and version discipline. And providers still realize the physical effect. This separation lets capability meaning remain durable across a change of model provider or deployment arrangement. It does not mean storing any JSON makes it trustworthy. The claim depends on which rows are authoritative, who can change them and how the runtime selects them.

About 65 seconds. Circuit mediation does not make isolation obsolete. The latest reviewed Windows source implements low-integrity execution by default and optional AppContainer execution. Later retained AppContainer receipts record acceptance, denied host writes and denied child-process launch. These controls are bounded: container-owned storage remains writable, and low-integrity mode has different residual access. The accepted quote and refused purchase shown earlier used different historical configurations. Do not combine them into a single imaginary hardened run. Independent evaluators should test the circuit, process environment and provider seam together on each supported host. Windows evidence is not proof of equivalent acceptance on every operating system.

S02: Reference monitor — CSRC Glossary. NIST. Undated glossary; definition cites SP 800-53 Rev. 5 (2020).
Supports: A reference validation mechanism should always mediate access, resist tampering, and be small enough for analysis and testing.
Limit: SideFX's non-bypassability, tamper resistance, and verifiability require implementation evidence.

About 85 seconds. This architecture should be assessable in concepts engineers already know. Complete mediation asks whether every effect path goes through the enforcement boundary. Fail-safe defaults ask what happens when declared authority is absent. Least privilege asks whether the inference side has more operational authority than it needs. Contracts make the required state explicit at boundaries. These are established principles, not new terminology invented to defend SideFX. The public challenge is to test how the actual circuit, executor and providers satisfy them. A principle appearing in this table does not certify the implementation or eliminate the need for bypass analysis.

About 65 seconds. Logical capability meaning need not belong to the physical machine that hosts a model or a client application. The same circuit vocabulary can support local invocation, an API service and remote providers. The kernel and providers still execute on actual machines. What moves is physical realization, while the declared capability remains the semantic reference. The API service has implemented run and evidence routes. A globally durable service, cross-platform acceptance and deployment-specific security are separate validation tasks. This is also the careful interpretation of the data-center thesis: an operable capability estate is an asset alongside compute, not a replacement for the need for hardware.

About 65 seconds. The architecture preserves the value of inference. Models can propose new ideas, drafts and candidate capabilities. The durable step is separate: evaluate the candidate, establish the required evidence and admit a declaration through controlled governance. Later requests can invoke that reusable capability instead of asking the model to reinvent the known procedure. Some capabilities will continue to call an inference provider because the task itself needs inference. The diagram is an architectural direction for governed improvement, not evidence that automatic admission or all formal proof stages are complete. Repetition alone does not turn a model result into a scientific fact.

About 75 seconds. Formal verification naturally fits this architecture, but we should reserve the term for an actual proof of an explicit property. A verifier can be a provider whose input contains a specification and implementation model and whose outcome supplies a proof artifact, counterexample or inconclusive result. Any proof is relative to the specification, model and assumptions. That result can feed a declared admission decision. A useful target invariant would relate every provider dispatch to an admitted circuit and matching binding. It must state the threat model and trusted assumptions. Today the retained runtime tests, schemas and digests establish narrower properties. They do not turn into a universal proof because we call them evidence. This is a concrete opportunity for research collaborators.

Supports: Refinement relates an implementation to a higher-level specification, while machine-checked proofs require work beyond informal correctness arguments.
Limit: Tests, hashes, deterministic execution, and provenance records are not themselves formal proofs.

S06: Certification Strategies using Run-Time Safety Assurance for Part 23 Autopilot Systems. Loyd R. Hook et al.; NASA Technical Reports Server. 2016-03-05.
Supports: Runtime verification and independent safety mechanisms can support assurance of complex autopilot behavior and supplement certification.
Limit: This is an engineering precedent, not evidence that SideFX has aviation certification or physical-control guarantees.

About 80 seconds. This slide makes the status legible. Retained runs demonstrate admitted execution and an undeclared purchase refusal. Reviewed source implements authority reads, explicit provider seams and addressed execution testimony. Later Windows receipts cover particular isolation configurations. These are substantial engineering results, but they are not the same as an independent security assessment, a complete caller authorization model, formal proof of the whole system or global production durability. Distinguishing those categories makes the next collaboration useful. We can ask partners to reproduce concrete behavior, look for bypasses and extend the assurance case, rather than asking them to accept a broad claim on confidence alone.

About 75 seconds. The collaboration should start with a concrete protocol. First reproduce the positive and negative paths from a pinned estate and runtime. Then attempt to cause effects through a missing capability, an overly broad admitted provider, hostile input, changed bindings and failure handling. Finally test operational realities: authority changes during a run, timeouts after a provider has acted, duplicate delivery, revoked credentials and tenant boundaries. We should record both whether a prohibited effect occurs and whether legitimate work is unnecessarily blocked. The targets here are proposed evaluation criteria, not measured success rates. NASA safety-case practice and the NIST AI RMF both support evidence-driven, continuing evaluation.
S07: Guidance on the Implementation of an Objectives-Driven, Risk-Informed, and Case-Assured Framework for Safety and Mission Success. NASA. 2025-03-03.
Supports: Safety assurance connects explicit risk objectives to an evolving argument supported by evidence throughout a program's lifecycle.
Limit: A demonstration alone does not establish a safety case across domains, hazards, and operating conditions.
S12: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0). NIST; Elham Tabassi. 2023-01-26.
Supports: The voluntary AI RMF organizes continuous risk work under Govern, Map, Measure, and Manage, including documented evaluation and limitations.
Limit: An architecture mapping is not NIST certification or complete framework compliance; a revision is in progress at access.

About 75 seconds. These are invitations, not announced partnerships. For OpenAI and Anthropic, the practical contribution would be diverse model behavior and adversarial prompt-injection tests against the same declared capability boundary. United States government evaluators can help define high-consequence test domains, assurance requirements and procurement-relevant evidence. The United Nations scientific and policy dialogue can support international comparison and inclusive discussion of the findings. Independent researchers can examine specifications, threat assumptions and proofs. The UN has established a Scientific Panel on AI and a Global Dialogue on AI Governance. SideFX can offer a reproducible engineering artifact for scrutiny within that larger effort, not claim to be its appointed solution.

S14: Independent International Scientific Panel on AI. United Nations. Established 2025-08-26 by A/RES/79/325; maintained page.
Supports: The UN established a scientific panel and Global Dialogue on AI Governance to connect independent scientific evidence with international deliberation.
Limit: Collaboration is an invitation, not an existing relationship; official indexed content was verified while direct pages used access protection.

Closing, about 45 seconds. We have built and demonstrated a specific execution boundary. The invitation is to challenge it, reproduce it and help extend it. A global solution will require reliable engineering, domain expertise, accountable governance and independent evidence across many organizations. SideFX offers a concrete architecture and retained execution artifacts with which that work can begin. The proposed first step is a joint reproduction and adversarial evaluation of a bounded capability set.
Visual: original generated conceptual scientific still life, 26 September 2026. It does not depict a real international agreement or event.

Technical appendix. The word capability is used here for an independently declared operational ability, not automatically for an unforgeable security token. Security literature has its own precise object-capability meaning. Provider and binding retain the same meaning at each level of composition. A model can be one provider inside a capability circuit.

Technical appendix. To claim that model data cannot open an undeclared operational path, the authority store and its change process must be protected, and all relevant effect paths must be mediated. The native executor and provider implementations are trusted components that need their own assessment. Existing capabilities can be overpowered or misused. Shape validation is not equivalent to caller, resource or tenant authorization. Provider-internal side effects and channels outside the controlled path remain separate subjects. These are conditions for evaluating the claim, not assertions that every listed failure has been observed in SideFX.

Supports: A reference validation mechanism should always mediate access, resist tampering, and be small enough for analysis and testing.

Technical appendix. A database transaction can keep related estate changes atomic, but it cannot automatically roll back a payment, message or physical action already performed by a remote provider. If a provider acts and its reply is lost, the runtime needs a declared way to reconcile what happened. Idempotency keys, retry policy, compensation and provider receipts are domain-specific engineering obligations. This slide states a validation requirement, not an assertion that one generic solution covers every provider. Evidence records the observed sequence and uncertainty rather than erasing that uncertainty.

Technical appendix. Capability security contributes a least-authority lens, but a business capability is not automatically an unforgeable security capability. They are neither claims of CHERI or PROV conformance nor NASA certification. Each correspondence should become a testable obligation in a joint evaluation.
